overview: White fianchettoes with g3, Bg2 and castles, then plays d3, Nbd2 and e4 against Black's ...c5 and ...d5 set-up (usually ...Nc6, ...e6, ...Nf6). Black has gained space on the queenside and plays ...Be7 and ...O-O or ...b5 ideas. The game is a slow manoeuvring battle where White aims for e4-e5 and a kingside attack and Black for queenside counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Bg2, O-O, d3, Nbd2 and e4, then e5 and a kingside attack
Re1, Nf1-e3 or h4-h5 for a kingside build-up

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Closed Sicilian / KID: White d3, e4 and g3 against Black c5, d5, e6

character.notes: Manoeuvring game with no forced theory; both sides can build slowly, so neither Solid nor Sharp.

soundness.notes: Sound; Fischer and Petrosian used the KIA.

structure.notes: Centre undecided with d3/e4 against c5/d5; could be closed or open later: flexible.

approach.notes: Same set-up against nearly any Black reply; KIA anchor is a system.

level.notes: Little to memorise, clear plans, but timing against ...d4 and ...b5 needs thought.

sublines_that_differ.name: KIA vs ...e6 French set-up
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d3 d5 3. Nd2 Nf6 4. Ngf3 c5 5. g3 Nc6 6. Bg2 Be7 7. O-O O-O 8. Re1
sublines_that_differ.how: Reached via the French move order; same plans.

character.reason: Slow manoeuvring game; attack comes later and is not forced.

soundness.reason: Established system used at all levels.

structure.reason: Centre stays undecided with d3 and ...c5/...d5.

approach.reason: KIA is a set-up played against nearly everything.

level.reason: Plans are clear but ...c5 lines ask for good timing; could be Beginner for White.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes then pushes e4-e5 to attack on the kingside.
